diagnostic_evidence.quote: Liouville’s formula provides an efficient integral representation for the log-determinant of the Jacobian

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed formula has the wrong trajectory and sign. For example, for the one-dimensional flow generated by v(x)=cx, change of variables gives log f_{Phi_*nu}(y)=log f_nu(e^{-c}y)-c, whereas the displayed right-hand side adds c. The divergence must be evaluated along the trajectory originating at Phi^{-1}(y), with the corresponding negative sign, or equivalently along a correctly parameterized backward trajectory.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by the correct Liouville/change-of-variables identity, including both the correct sign and trajectory.
issues.overall_effect: The stated likelihood representation used to motivate likelihood-based training is false as written, although later arguments generally revert to the Jacobian change-of-variables formula.
issues.title: Incorrect Liouville density formula
issues.why_classification: This is a local formula correction that preserves the likelihood method and does not require changing subsequent substantive guarantees.

Consequently the full derivative DT need not exist at every x, so the pointwise determinant identity is not justified under the theorem's hypotheses.

The paper's Clenshaw-Curtis node formula is undefined at m=1 because it divides by m-1. Moreover, for d>1 the stated error bound has a zero right-hand side because log 1=0, although a one-point quadrature rule is not exact for all C^k functions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The target class $\mathcal{T} \subset \mathcal{M}_1^+([0,1]^d)$ consists of absolutely continuous measures with densities $f_\mu \in C^k([0,1]^d)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership of each density in C^k together with uniform upper and lower value bounds does not give a uniform C^k norm bound. Densities such as 1+a sin(2 pi N x), with fixed sufficiently small a, retain common positive upper and lower bounds while their derivatives grow without bound as N increases. Thus the proof's uniform bound on the target vector fields, and hence the architecture-independent approximation constants asserted for all targets, do not follow from the assumptions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a uniform C^k or C^{k-1,1} norm bound to the definition of the target class and propagate that bound through all constants and thresholds; otherwise replace the uniform conclusions by target-dependent ones.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform model-error rate and the uniform PAC guarantee over the stated target class are unsupported. In fact, the class permits arbitrarily fine oscillations with no common complexity control.

issues.failure_explanation: The logarithm of the determinant is not controlled solely by the absolute matrix difference. Already in dimension one, A=epsilon and B=2epsilon give |log A-log B|=log 2 while the asserted right-hand side tends to zero with epsilon. A valid estimate needs quantitative lower singular-value bounds or factors involving inverse matrices. The same invalid inequality is reused in the model-error, sub-Gaussian, and concentration arguments.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Establish uniform lower singular-value bounds for all relevant flow Jacobians and prove a correctly conditioned log-determinant estimate, or rebuild the estimates using the divergence integral along the flow.
issues.overall_effect: The KL model-error estimate and the determinant portions of both generalization estimates are not proved, so their downstream PAC bound is unreliable.
issues.title: False determinant sensitivity inequality
issues.why_classification: Flow bounds may support a comparable corrected estimate, but the repair requires a nontrivial matrix/ODE lemma and must be propagated through several constants.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:lip_constants controls changes in the network parameter at a fixed input. In the quoted application, both the parameter and the spatial evaluation point change. The omitted spatial term requires control of the Lipschitz modulus of D_x v, equivalently a suitable uniform second-derivative or C^{1,1} bound, together with a flow-position stability estimate. The concentration proof repeats the same unsupported spatial control even with the parameter fixed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove uniform architecture-dependent C^{1,1} or second-derivative bounds for the ReQU vector fields, split parameter and spatial variations correctly, and redo the flow and growth estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed sub-Gaussian increment metric and bounded-difference constant are unproved, invalidating both probabilistic generalization estimates and their use in the main theorem.
issues.title: Parameter Lipschitz bound is incorrectly applied at different spatial points
issues.why_classification: A comparable result may be obtainable from the piecewise-quadratic architecture, but it requires a new nontrivial regularity lemma and rederivation of the capacity-dependent constants.

issues.failure_explanation: By definition the generalization error is sup_theta |Z_theta,n|, not sup_theta Z_theta,n. Moreover, an increment-only Dudley bound controls a process relative to an anchor and does not by itself control the random value at that anchor. The proof supplies neither the negative-process argument nor an anchor estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the entropy argument to both Z and -Z and add a bounded estimate for one fixed anchor parameter, adjusting the numerical constant.
issues.overall_effect: The stated expected generalization bound, and hence the centering used by the concentration theorem and main proof, is not established with the claimed argument.
issues.title: Dudley argument does not control the absolute empirical process
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local empirical-process repair that should preserve the n^{-1/2} rate and all qualitative guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any architecture parameters $L_n, W_n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, it is possible to choose a threshold $m(n)$ for the number of quadrature points
provided also that the number of quadrature points $m \geq m(n^*)$ is sufficiently large.

issues.failure_explanation: The quadrature estimate contains an architecture-dependent C^1 bound that grows with L_n and W_n. The proof therefore obtains, for each n, a threshold m(n). It then fixes m(n*) at the initial sample threshold and claims this controls every n>=n*, but no monotonicity in the needed direction or uniform bound is shown; the displayed architecture factor instead grows as n increases. Thus a fixed m>=m(n*) need not control the quadrature error for a much larger n.
